exposure: Fetal growth classification based on universal standard growth charts
Fetal growth classification based on local population-based growth chart
outcome: Birth weight to placental weight ratio
Rate of villitis of unknown etiology
cohort: Singleton deliveries from 2008 to 2019, categorized into: small-for-gestational-age (SGA) neonates according to the local population-based chart, SGA according to universal standard growth charts (but appropriate for gestational age [AGA] according to local charts), and AGA deliveries according to both charts
finding: Using a local population-based growth chart identified a group of SGA neonates with a higher risk of adverse outcomes, including preterm delivery, cesarean delivery, lower placental weight, higher birth weight to placental weight ratio, and a higher rate of maternal malperfusion lesions.
mod_finding: The study found that the local population small-for-gestational-age group had a significantly higher rate of preterm and cesarean deliveries.
